Mykolayivka-Novorossiyska Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Mykolaivka-Novorosiiska, Ukraine

Demolished. This cemetery's founding is undocumented, though it appears on a 1923 Russian map using 1916 data; per Yizkor accounts, it was entirely destroyed and its land plowed during WWII. Jewish community mentions date to the mid-19th century; population reached 980 (36%) by 1897, with a synagogue built 1844 and a Hevra Kadisha operating from 1858, alongside societies caring for the sick and poor. A Hasidic synagogue opened in 1890, the same year a Hebrew school was founded by Rabbi M. Rebelsky (active 1904-1911). During an October 1905 pogrom, two members of a Jewish self-defense detachment were killed. Population reached 806 (29%) by 1930. Most Jews were deported to Transnistria in late June-early July 1941; the remaining 80 residents were murdered that August.
